q: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
e: Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India; he was succeeded by C. Rajagopalachari, the first Indian to hold the post.

q: The quorum required for a sitting of the Lok Sabha is:

options.A: One-fifth of the total number of members
options.B: One-fourth of the total number of members
options.C: One-eighth of the total number of members
options.D: One-tenth of the total number of members

e: The quorum required for a sitting of the Lok Sabha is one-tenth of the total number of its members, as laid down in Article 100.

q: Most of the edicts of Emperor Ashoka were inscribed in which script?
e: Most of the edicts of Emperor Ashoka were inscribed in the Brahmi script; Kharoshthi was used only in the north-western parts.

q: In the First Battle of Tarain (1191), Muhammad Ghori was defeated by:
e: In the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, Muhammad Ghori was defeated by the Rajput ruler Prithviraj Chauhan, though Ghori won the second battle in 1192.

q: The Fourth Buddhist Council, held in Kashmir, was convened under the patronage of the Kushana ruler:
e: The Fourth Buddhist Council, held in Kashmir, was convened under the patronage of the Kushana ruler Kanishka.

q: Shivaji was crowned as Chhatrapati at Raigad Fort in the year:
e: Shivaji was crowned as Chhatrapati in a formal coronation ceremony at Raigad Fort in the year 1674.

q: Todar Mal, famous for his land revenue reforms, was the revenue minister of the Mughal emperor:
e: Todar Mal, famous for his land revenue reforms including the zabt system, was the revenue minister of the Mughal emperor Akbar.

q: Mangal Pandey, the sepoy whose act of defiance in March 1857 preceded the great revolt, was stationed at:
e: Mangal Pandey, the sepoy whose defiance in March 1857 preceded the great revolt, was stationed at Barrackpore near Calcutta.

q: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between:

options.A: The Indian National Congress and the Muslim League
options.B: The Indian National Congress and the British Government
options.C: The Hindu Mahasabha and the Muslim League
options.D: The Indian National Congress and the Arya Samaj

e: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League for a joint scheme of constitutional reforms.

q: The Government of India Act, 1935 is best known for providing:
e: The Government of India Act, 1935 is best known for providing provincial autonomy, ending dyarchy in the provinces.

q: The largest district of India by area is:
e: Kachchh district in Gujarat, covering about 45,000 square kilometres, is the largest district of India by area.

q: Which Indian State shares the longest international border with a neighbouring country?
e: West Bengal shares the longest international border, its boundary of over 2,200 km with Bangladesh being the longest for any Indian State.

q: The largest plateau in the world is the:
e: The Tibetan Plateau, often called the Roof of the World, is the largest and highest plateau in the world.

q: The Panama Canal connects which two oceans?

options.A: The Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean
options.B: The Atlantic Ocean and the Indian Ocean
options.C: The Pacific Ocean and the Indian Ocean
options.D: The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea

e: The Panama Canal, built across the isthmus of Panama, connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean.

q: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak of Africa, is located in:
e: Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak of Africa at about 5,895 metres, is located in Tanzania.

q: The longest mountain range in the world is the:
e: The Andes, running along the western coast of South America for several thousand kilometres, is the longest mountain range in the world.

q: Which river discharges the largest volume of water into the sea?
e: The Amazon river discharges the largest volume of water into the sea, far more than any other river of the world.

q: 'Dakshin Gangotri' is best known as:

options.B: India's first research station in Antarctica

e: Dakshin Gangotri was India's first research station in Antarctica, established there in 1983-84.

q: The 'Loo', experienced over the northern plains of India in summer, is:

options.A: A cold wave blowing in winter
options.B: A monsoon wind from the Bay of Bengal
options.C: A cool sea breeze along the coast
options.D: A hot and dry wind blowing during the day

e: The Loo is a hot and dry wind that blows during the day over the northern plains of India in the summer season.

q: The Union Budget of India is presented in the Lok Sabha by the:
e: The Union Budget is presented in the Lok Sabha by the Finance Minister of the Government of India.

q: The financial year of the Government of India runs from:
e: The financial year of the Government of India runs from 1 April to 31 March of the following year.

q: The headquarters of the World Bank is located at:
e: The headquarters of the World Bank is located at Washington D.C., the capital of the United States of America.

q: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was set up as a result of the conference held in 1944 at:
e: The International Monetary Fund was set up as a result of the United Nations monetary conference held in 1944 at Bretton Woods.

q: The first Census of India was conducted in the year 1872 during the viceroyalty of:
e: The first Census of India was conducted in 1872 during the viceroyalty of Lord Mayo.

q: The term 'Hindu rate of growth', used for the slow growth of the Indian economy in the early decades after Independence, was coined by the economist:
e: The term Hindu rate of growth, for the slow growth of the Indian economy in the early decades after Independence, was coined by the economist Raj Krishna.

q: The Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) was established in the year:
e: The Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) was established in 1956, when the life insurance business in India was nationalised.

q: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the:
e: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the ohm, named after the German physicist Georg Simon Ohm.

q: The largest organ of the human body is the:
e: The skin, which covers the whole body and protects it, is the largest organ of the human body.

q: Which blood group is known as the 'universal recipient' group?
e: The AB positive blood group is known as the universal recipient group because a person of this group can receive blood from all other groups.

q: The hormone insulin, which regulates the blood sugar level, is secreted by the:
e: Insulin, the hormone that regulates the blood sugar level, is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas.

q: Malaria is transmitted to human beings by the bite of the:
e: Malaria is transmitted to human beings by the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito, which carries the malaria parasite.

q: The World Wide Web (WWW) was invented by:
e: The World Wide Web (WWW) was invented by Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist working at CERN, in 1989.

q: The solar system of which the Earth is a part belongs to the galaxy called:
e: The solar system, including the Earth, is a part of the galaxy called the Milky Way.

q: Acid rain is caused mainly by the presence in the atmosphere of the oxides of:
e: Acid rain is caused mainly by the oxides of sulphur and nitrogen released into the atmosphere, which dissolve in rain water to form acids.

q: The Sanskrit work 'Buddhacharita', a biography of Gautama Buddha, was composed by:
e: The Sanskrit work Buddhacharita, an epic biography of Gautama Buddha, was composed by the poet Ashvaghosha.

q: The 'Ramcharitmanas', the famous retelling of the Ramayana in Awadhi, was composed by:
e: The Ramcharitmanas, the famous retelling of the Ramayana in the Awadhi language, was composed by the saint-poet Tulsidas.

q: The novel 'The God of Small Things', which won the Booker Prize, was written by:
e: The novel The God of Small Things, which won the Booker Prize in 1997, was written by Arundhati Roy.

q: The Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in sports was instituted in the year:
e: The Arjuna Award for outstanding performance in sports and games was instituted in the year 1961.

q: National Sports Day is celebrated in India every year on:
e: National Sports Day is celebrated in India on 29 August every year, the birthday of the hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

q: The Wimbledon tennis championship, the oldest tennis tournament in the world, is played on courts of:
e: The Wimbledon championship, the oldest tennis tournament in the world, is played on grass courts, the only Grand Slam event still held on grass.

q: The Samastipur division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Samastipur division in Bihar is a part of the East Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Hajipur.

q: The Vadodara division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Vadodara division, covering Vadodara and Bharuch in Gujarat, belongs to the Western Railway.

q: The Jaipur division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Jaipur division is administered by the North Western Railway, which has its headquarters at Jaipur itself.

q: The Bilaspur division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Bilaspur division is a part of the South East Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Bilaspur.

q: The Secunderabad division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Secunderabad division, one of the largest divisions of Indian Railways, belongs to the South Central Railway.

q: The Hyderabad division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Hyderabad division is administered by the South Central Railway headquartered at Secunderabad.

q: The Raipur division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Raipur division in Chhattisgarh is a part of the South East Central Railway headquartered at Bilaspur.

q: The Ajmer division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Ajmer division, covering Ajmer and parts of Rajasthan, belongs to the North Western Railway.

q: The Purushottam Express, a popular superfast train from Odisha, runs between Puri and:
e: The Purushottam Express, a popular superfast train from Odisha, runs between Puri and New Delhi.

q: The Konkan Kanya Express runs between Mumbai CSMT and:
e: The Konkan Kanya Express runs between Mumbai CSMT and Madgaon in Goa along the Konkan Railway route.

q: The Mandovi Express, running between Mumbai and Goa, derives its name from:

options.B: A hill range in the Western Ghats
options.D: The first Chief Minister of Goa

e: The train takes its name from the Mandovi, the principal river of Goa, which flows past Panaji before joining the Arabian Sea.

q: The Godavari Express, a well-known train of the Telugu States, runs between Hyderabad and:
e: The Godavari Express links Hyderabad with Visakhapatnam, the port city of Andhra Pradesh, and is named after the river Godavari.

q: The Ashram Express, named after the Sabarmati Ashram, runs between Ahmedabad and:
e: The Ashram Express connects Ahmedabad, home of Gandhiji's Sabarmati Ashram after which it is named, with Delhi.

q: The Swaraj Express, a long-distance superfast train, runs between Bandra Terminus (Mumbai) and:
e: The Swaraj Express is a superfast service between Bandra Terminus in Mumbai and Jammu Tawi.

q: The historic Gujarat Mail, among the oldest trains of Western Railway, runs between Mumbai Central and:
e: The Gujarat Mail is one of the oldest trains of Western Railway and runs between Mumbai Central and Ahmedabad.

q: In Indian Railways, 'ATVM', the self-service machines provided at stations for issuing unreserved tickets, stands for:
e: ATVM stands for Automatic Ticket Vending Machine, the self-service machines at stations that issue unreserved tickets against smart cards or cash.

q: In the Freight Operations Information System (FOIS) of Indian Railways, the module 'TMS', which handles transactions at goods terminals, stands for:
e: In FOIS, TMS is the Terminal Management System, which captures loading, unloading and other transactions at goods terminals.

q: In the Freight Operations Information System (FOIS) of Indian Railways, the module 'RMS', which deals with the planning and movement of rakes, stands for:
e: In FOIS, RMS is the Rake Management System, which deals with the planning, placement and movement of freight rakes.

q: The full form of IRSEE, an organised Group 'A' service of Indian Railways, is:

options.B: Indian Railway Service of Electrical Engineers
options.C: Indian Railway Signal and Electrical Engineering Service
options.D: Indian Railway Service of Electronics Engineers

e: IRSEE is the Indian Railway Service of Electrical Engineers, the organised Group A service for the electrical department of the Railways.

q: 'Meri Saheli', an initiative of Indian Railways launched through the Railway Protection Force, is primarily concerned with:

options.C: The safety and security of women passengers travelling by train

e: Meri Saheli is an RPF initiative under which teams assist and ensure the safety and security of women passengers travelling by train.

q: Under the 'guarantee system' followed for railway construction in India in the nineteenth century, the British private companies building the railways were assured by the Government of:

options.A: Exemption from all land acquisition costs
options.B: A minimum return (interest) on the capital invested by them
options.C: Monopoly rights over all trade along the railway lines
options.D: Free supply of locomotives and rolling stock

e: Under the guarantee system, the British companies building railways in India were assured a minimum return of interest on their invested capital, whatever the earnings.

q: The famous 'Railway Minute' of 1853, which laid down the broad policy for the construction of railways in India, was written by:
e: The Railway Minute of 1853, which laid down the broad framework for railway construction in India, was written by Governor-General Lord Dalhousie.

q: Tram services, which once operated in several Indian cities, survive today in regular operation only in the city of:
e: Trams survive in regular operation in India only in Kolkata, where the system has run since 1873.

q: The 'F-734', turned out in 1895 and regarded as the first steam locomotive built in India, was manufactured at the railway workshop at:
e: The F-734 of 1895, regarded as the first steam locomotive built in India, was turned out by the railway workshop at Ajmer.

q: In railway track terminology, 'creep' refers to:

options.A: The gradual longitudinal movement of rails in the track
options.B: The wearing away of the rail head by wheel flanges
options.C: The settlement of ballast under repeated loading
options.D: The widening of gauge on sharp curves

e: Creep is the gradual longitudinal movement of rails in the direction of traffic, caused by wheel action and temperature effects.

q: The treads of railway wheels are 'coned', that is, given a slight slope, primarily in order to:

options.A: Reduce the weight of the wheel
options.B: Help the wheelset remain centred on the track and negotiate curves smoothly
options.C: Increase the grip of the wheel on wet rails
options.D: Make the wheels interchangeable between gauges

e: Coned wheel treads give the wheelset a self-centring action, keeping it aligned on the track and helping it negotiate curves smoothly.

q: A 'catch siding' provided on a steep gradient section of a railway line is meant to:

options.A: Park inspection trolleys clear of the running line
options.B: Hold spare wagons for emergency loading
options.C: Store engineering materials near work sites
options.D: Divert and arrest vehicles that may run away down the gradient

e: A catch siding on a steep gradient is provided to divert and arrest wagons or vehicles that escape and run away down the grade.

q: During foggy weather, detonators are placed on the rail head in the vicinity of signals primarily to:

options.A: Test whether the track circuit is working
options.B: Frighten away animals from the track
options.C: Warn the loco pilot, through the sound of the explosion under the wheels, that a signal is being approached
options.D: Mark the exact stopping point for the train

e: Detonators exploded under the wheels during fog audibly warn the loco pilot that he is approaching a signal, when visibility is poor.

q: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, which climbs from the plains to the hill station of Darjeeling, negotiates its steep climb mainly with the help of:

options.A: Rack and pinion assistance throughout its length
options.C: Cable haulage on the steepest stretches
options.D: Additional banking locomotives at every station

e: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway climbs its steep gradient mainly through loops and zig-zag reverses or switchbacks, without rack assistance.

q: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory, a coach manufacturing unit of Indian Railways in Maharashtra, is located at:
e: The Marathwada Rail Coach Factory of Indian Railways is located at Latur in Maharashtra.

q: The Kottavalasa-Kirandul (KK) railway line of Indian Railways is primarily known for carrying:

options.A: Iron ore from the Bailadila mines to Visakhapatnam
options.B: Coal from the Talcher coalfields to Paradip

e: The Kottavalasa-Kirandul line carries iron ore from the Bailadila mines of Chhattisgarh down to the port of Visakhapatnam.

q: The Pipavav Railway Corporation Limited, which executed the first public-private partnership (PPP) project of Indian Railways, provides rail connectivity to:
e: Pipavav Railway Corporation Limited, the first PPP project of Indian Railways, provides rail connectivity to Pipavav Port in Gujarat.

q: Shinjuku station, generally regarded as the busiest railway station in the world by passenger numbers, is located in the city of:
e: Shinjuku in Tokyo is generally regarded as the busiest railway station in the world by daily passenger numbers.

q: The 'Eurostar' high-speed passenger train services connect London, through the Channel Tunnel, with:
e: Eurostar high-speed trains run from London through the Channel Tunnel to Paris and Brussels.

q: The underground railway system of London, the oldest metro system in the world, is popularly nicknamed:
e: The London Underground, the oldest metro system in the world, opened in 1863, is popularly nicknamed the Tube.

q: The 'Rocket', which won the famous Rainhill Trials of 1829 and marked a landmark in steam locomotive development, was built by:
e: The Rocket, built by George Stephenson, won the Rainhill Trials of 1829 and proved the practicality of the steam locomotive.

q: The longest metro rail network in the world, by route length, is the metro system of:
e: The Shanghai Metro has the longest route length of any metro system in the world.

q: The 'Ghan', a famous long-distance passenger train running between Adelaide and Darwin, belongs to which country?
e: The Ghan is Australia's famous long-distance train, running between Adelaide in the south and Darwin in the north.

q: The largest metro rail network in India, by route length, is the:
e: The Delhi Metro has the largest metro rail network in India by route length.

q: In terms of route length, the smallest zonal railway of Indian Railways is the:
e: Metro Railway, Kolkata, is the smallest zonal railway of Indian Railways in terms of route length.

q: The Naranarayan Setu, a rail-cum-road bridge in Assam near Jogighopa, is built across the river:
e: The Naranarayan Setu near Jogighopa in Assam is a rail-cum-road bridge built across the Brahmaputra.

q: The Farakka Bridge in West Bengal, which carries rail and road traffic over a barrage, is built across the river:
e: The Farakka Bridge, which carries rail and road traffic over the Farakka Barrage in West Bengal, is built across the Ganga.

q: The Manduadih railway station near Varanasi was renamed in 2020 as:
e: Manduadih station near Varanasi was renamed Banaras in 2020, restoring its older name.

q: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway is the only railway in India which climbs its steep gradients with the help of:
e: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway is the only railway in India using a rack and pinion (Abt) system to climb its steep gradients.

q: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway, opened in 1830 in England, is regarded as the world's first:
e: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway of 1830 is regarded as the world's first inter-city passenger railway.

q: The Emergency provisions in the Constitution of India have been borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The Emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Weimar Constitution of Germany.

q: Who was the first woman to become the Chief Minister of an Indian State?
e: Sucheta Kripalani became the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian State when she took office in Uttar Pradesh in 1963.

q: The minimum age prescribed for a person to be appointed as the Governor of a State in India is:
e: Under the Constitution, a person must have completed 35 years of age to be appointed Governor of a State.

q: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the President of India to seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on a question of law or fact of public importance?
e: Article 143 empowers the President to refer questions of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its advisory opinion.

q: The doctrine of the 'basic structure' of the Constitution was laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of:

options.A: Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala (1973)
options.C: A. K. Gopalan vs State of Madras (1950)
options.D: Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras (1950)

e: The basic structure doctrine was laid down by the Supreme Court in Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala in 1973, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.

q: In the Lok Sabha, the Speaker exercises a 'casting vote':

options.B: Only when there is an equality of votes
options.C: Whenever the House is in disorder

e: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha exercises a casting vote only when the votes for and against a motion are exactly equal.

q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council is chaired by the:

options.B: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Finance Minister of the host State

e: The GST Council, set up under Article 279A, is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

q: The capital of the Mauryan Empire was:
e: Pataliputra, near modern Patna, was the capital of the Mauryan Empire of Chandragupta and Ashoka.

q: In the Battle of Karnal (1739), the Mughal forces were defeated by:
e: In the Battle of Karnal in 1739, the Persian ruler Nadir Shah defeated the Mughal forces and went on to plunder Delhi.

q: The Banaras Hindu University, founded in 1916, was established by:
e: Banaras Hindu University, founded in 1916, was established by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya.

q: The famous trials of the officers of the Indian National Army (INA) in 1945 were held at:
e: The famous trials of INA officers in 1945 were held at the Red Fort in Delhi.

q: The Treaty of Versailles, signed in 1919, formally brought to an end the:
e: The Treaty of Versailles of 1919 formally ended the First World War between Germany and the Allied Powers.

q: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations?
e: Trygve Lie of Norway was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations, serving from 1946.

q: The ancient university of Vikramshila, a renowned centre of learning, was founded by the Pala ruler:
e: The ancient university of Vikramshila was founded by the Pala ruler Dharmapala, as a great centre of Buddhist learning.

q: The Pitt's India Act, which established the Board of Control to supervise the East India Company, was passed in the year:
e: Pitt's India Act of 1784 created the Board of Control to supervise the East India Company's affairs in India.
